newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Iceland Energy in aluminium smelter talks with US.
newsitem.headline: Iceland Energy in aluminium smelter talks with US.

text.p: Iceland's energy marketing body said on Monday it was in the final stages of negotiations with a U.S. company over a possible second aluminium smelter for Iceland.
Gardar Ingvarsson, managing director of the Icelandic Energy Marketing Agency, said talks with U.S. company Columbia Ventures Corp continued in earnest in August.
He said he would travel to New York this week for further talks.
No announcement has yet been made on whether the U.S. group, run by U.S. lawyer Kenneth Peterson, has chosen Iceland or Venezuela as the site of a 60,000 tonnes per year smelter.
"We are in earnest negotiations and hopeful of a final decision soon," Ingvarsson told Reuters by telephone from Reykjavik.
Iceland has abundant power supplies, with only about 10 percent of its capacity currently used, but Venezuela had been offering electric power 50 percent cheaper.
Iceland currently has one aluminium smelter run by Swiss-based Alusuisse-Lonza Holdings AG.
This is currently undergoing a two-year, $200 million expansion project to boost capacity to 160,000 tonnes a year from 100,000 tonnes.
Another aluminium smelter project is currently under review for Iceland.

A consortium involving Dutch Hoogovens NV, Sweden's Electrolux-owned Granges and U.S. aluminium producer and processor Alumax Inc, is considering a 220,000 tonne a year smelter project with room to double capacity.
Ingvarsson said a decision was expected to be made by the end of the year.
